Create Column Structure for a J&J-Style Shift Table

Source: R/risk_diff_col_struct.R
shift_tbl_col_struct.Rd

Create Column Structure for a J&J-Style Shift Table

Usage

shift_tbl_col_struct(lyt, var, span_lbl = "Baseline", .outer_spl_var = var)

Arguments

lyt

(PreDataTableLayouts)
The layout, typically as returned directly from basic_table.

var

(character(1))
The variable defining the partition to create a shift table for.

span_lbl

(character(1))
The spanning label for the shift portion of the column structure. Defaults to "Baseline".

.outer_spl_var

(character(1))
The variable to "split on" when creating the spanning labels. Must exist in the dataset(s) used in build_table but its values are irrelevant.

Value

lyt updated with the specified shift table column structure.

Details

This function creates a column structure akin to the following (with Grade 1 through Grade 5 representing the levels of var):

                              Baseline
  N   Grade 1   Grade 2   Grade 3   Grade 4   Grade 5   Total
——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————

See also

Other std_col_struct: grouped_cols_w_diffs(), make_multicomp_splfun()

Examples

shift_data <- data.frame(
  BASE = factor(c("Grade 1", "Grade 2", "Grade 3")),
  CHG = c("Improved", "Stable", "Worsened")
)

lyt <- basic_table() |>
  shift_tbl_col_struct("BASE") |>
  analyze("CHG", afun = function(x, ...) length(x))

build_table(lyt, shift_data)
#>                        Baseline              
#>       N   Grade 1   Grade 2   Grade 3   Total
#> —————————————————————————————————————————————
#> CHG   3      1         1         1        3
